title: On which day was the doubling pond half covered?
description: A pond starts with one lotus and the number doubles every day until it is full on day thirty. Going back one day halves the lotuses, and each count is written as a power of two. Keeko's doubt is that half of thirty days is fifteen days.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a count doubles every day, the day before full it is half, and the count has one fewer two multiplied. Watch for students who halve the number of days instead of going back one day.

source: A pond starts with 1 lotus and the number doubles every day.
video_script.why: The child can write repeated multiplication as a power and now follows a count that doubles every day.
video_script.substitution: The book's own magical pond, with one lotus at the start, doubling every day and full after thirty days.
video_script.anchor: a pond on the board with one lotus at the start, and the lotus count doubling day by day up to day thirty
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks half of thirty is fifteen, so the pond is half covered on day fifteen. One more doubling from half covered would fill the pond on day sixteen, not day thirty.
video_script.payoff_line: The pond was half covered on day twenty nine

final_answer.value: Day 29; 2 to the power 30 lotuses when full and 2 to the power 29 when half covered
final_answer.spoken: day twenty nine; two to the power thirty lotuses when full and two to the power twenty nine when half covered

maths_rules: day 0: 1 lotus; each day × 2; after n days 2ⁿ lotuses
the day before full is half: day 30 − 1 = 29
slip: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 halves the days; if day 15 were half covered, day 16 would be full
video_script.design: One idea: going back one day halves a doubling count. The pond stays on the board all video; the day and the half count are left open until the answer; one slip at the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a magical pond.
<bookmark mark='pond'/>A pond starts with one lotus, and the number of lotuses doubles every day.
The pond is completely covered after thirty days.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>On which day was it half covered?
And how many lotuses were there when it was full, and when it was half covered?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.double: an arrow marked × 2 appears between the days
marks.adds: one more 2 is added each day

narration: <bookmark mark='double'/>Doubling means multiplying by two.
<bookmark mark='three'/>After three days, one lotus becomes eight lotuses, which is two cubed.
<bookmark mark='adds'/>Each day adds one more two to the multiplication.

marks.given: 1 lotus at the start and doubles every day are written

<bookmark mark='full'/>The pond is full after thirty days.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the day it was half covered.
<bookmark mark='count'/>We also need the number of lotuses when full and when half covered.

beats.on_screen: doubles each day, so one day back halves the lotuses; half covered is one day before full; day 30 − 1 = ?

marks.one: an arrow marked × 2 forward and ÷ 2 backward is drawn
marks.half: the day before full is marked half covered
marks.open: 30 − 1 = ? is written with the result left open

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, each day the lotuses double, so each day back halves them.
<bookmark mark='half'/>One day before full, the pond is half covered.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Counting back one day from day thirty is left to find.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, count the lotuses when full.
One lotus doubles thirty times.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>That is thirty twos multiplied, which is two to the power thirty.

beats.on_screen: half covered: one doubling fewer, so one fewer 2; 30 − 1 = ?

marks.three: half covered is marked one doubling fewer
marks.fewer: one 2 is struck from the row of thirty twos
marks.open: 30 − 1 = ? is written with the result left open

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, count the lotuses when half covered.
<bookmark mark='fewer'/>That is one doubling fewer, so there is one fewer two multiplied.
<bookmark mark='open'/>Thirty twos take away one two is left to find.

beats.on_screen: Answer: day 29; half covered 2²⁹ lotuses; full 2³⁰ lotuses; 2²⁹ × 2 = 2³⁰
narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>The pond was half covered on day twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>It held two to the power twenty nine lotuses then.
When full, it held two to the power thirty lotuses.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Doubling the half gives the full, because twenty nine twos and one more two make thirty twos.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the pond
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 and day 15 appear, then are crossed out; day 15 half covered would make day 16 full

marks.count: day 15 is shown half covered, and one doubling later day 16 is shown full
marks.fix: day 15 is crossed out and the half covered mark moves to one day before day 30

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks half of thirty is fifteen, so it is half covered on day fifteen.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But if the pond were half covered on that day, one more doubling would fill it.
That would make it full on day sixteen, not day thirty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The lotuses double each day, so the pond is half covered one day before full.
